newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NEWCASTLE SUFFER SETBACK AT NOTTINGHAM FOREST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEWCASTLE SUFFER SETBACK AT NOTTINGHAM FOREST.

text.p: Newcastle's hopes of slotting into second place behind English league leaders Arsenal backfired on Monday when they were held 0-0 at lowly Nottingham Forest.
The draw lifted Newcastle from fifth to fourth ahead of Aston Villa but they now trail the London pacesetters by five points.
Forest showed great fighting spirit and, in a game of many chances, Alfie Haaland went closest to breaking the deadlock nine minutes from time when he rattled the post.

Forest's point lifted them off the bottom of the premier league -- they moved above Coventry having scored more goals -- but it left them without a league win since the opening day of the season and without a home league success in eight attempts.
It was Newcastle's first goalless draw in 74 games, a run stretching back to their stalemate against Manchester City on April 29 1995.
Not even the re-appearance of Newcastle strike pairing of Alan Shearer and Les Ferdinand could inspire a much-needed win.
Ferdinand, back after injury, was off target with near-post headers in either half and volleyed over from Shearer's nod down in first-half injury time.
Newcastle lined up without the suspended David Batty and the inspirational Colombian Faustino Asprilla, sidelined by a hamstring strain.
